decisions.finding: Two manual CLIs, one authenticated API and a server-only helper had independent transport/normalization. Domain-only checks and bearer authentication did not establish indexing, fact, locale or owner approval. No current application callers of the helper or CI invocations of manual CLIs were found in the audited tree.
decisions.action: One pure shared canonical URL/pause policy; remove outbound transport from all four current entrypoints. Runtime pause is source-controlled and has no environment/force bypass. Do not change the public key file, authentication requirements or deploy secret policy.

decisions.finding: Historical priority arrays include withdrawn global character/guide/tool URLs. Added shared version templates were expanded to every core game without proving public URL existence, and the old new-pages script had no dry-run mode.
decisions.action: Preserve the historical priority candidate set for explicit comparison, not approval. Both CLIs now default to offline plans; reject --submit and unknown arguments. New-page candidates must be explicit --path/--url; remove Git-template expansion and its fragile direct Node import of the TypeScript package.

Optional explicit local XML urlset snapshots parsed with Python ElementTree, namespace/type/size/duplicate/canonical validation and file digests. No regex loc extraction, URL fetching, owner auto-expansion or implicit default evidence. Distinguish listed/not-listed/not-assessed; every candidate remains submissionAllowed=false. Missing owners and stale snapshots never count as whole-site approval.

Keep missing-secret 503 and wrong-bearer 401; malformed/noncanonical batches are 400. Authenticated valid requests now explicitly return paused 503/ok=false, never misleading notified success. Compatibility helpers retain async void/non-throwing signatures, validate all-or-nothing and log paused state without sending HTTP.

Reject compiled code containing known legacy IndexNow transport endpoint strings before starting an authenticated local fixture. Use only a hardcoded synthetic local token and loopback requests to test API denial; no production credential or target search request is used.

limitations: No request sent to production or any search-engine endpoint; local snapshot membership is not live page/robots/canonical/owner-completeness approval.

This is an intentional site-wide pause of discovery/promotion transports, not a claim that IndexNow forbids change/removal notifications for noindex URLs. Removal notification is a separate unimplemented workflow.
Pause does not withdraw previously submitted URLs or immediately change search results; code is local only until separately released.
Runtime/API/helper and manual-script policy changes do not repair remaining Roco redeem-code claims or generic item Coming Soon routes. They are explicitly recorded as remaining content risks.
Two factual holds, raw/public data, old assets and registration/deployment configuration stay unchanged; no new official global evidence or artwork permission obtained.
Future resumption requires separately implemented production preflight/approval and cross-owner acceptance; closing holds or flipping an environment variable must not auto-enable sending.

readOnlyFollowups.finding: Empty stored international material list; generic items also empty, and web item adapters have no roco case. This is not proof that the game has no items.
Empty stored international redeem-code list; the actual public codes page still renders a separate hardcoded RocoRedeemHub. Raw emptiness does not withdraw page-level claims.

Reachable hardcoded hub still publishes 2026-10-27 testing priority, CBT/platform/reward categories, an active-code zero, and official-source endorsements. It is still included in current local sitemap. Highest next content batch: archive/correct this whole consumer boundary; not edited or newly fact-verified here.

No dedicated roco renderer; generic fallback outputs Coming Soon even when registry items is false. Do not infer a 404 or safety merely from the route flag; direct route HTTP/metadata needs a bounded follow-up.
